name: control-arm-fifteen
purpose: The first control arm. Every LibreCalc result so far is measured against LibreCalc; this asks whether the interface buys anything at all against the harness the benchmark ships with -- bash, view_xlsx, openpyxl/pandas/LibreOffice, the official prompt. Same model and same tasks in both arms. Run it with --control for the baseline and without for ours, then compare exact counts and mean accuracies, not single tasks.
sampling: Deterministic and drawn before any result was seen: within each category, task ids sorted and five taken at evenly spaced positions, with the 15 contaminated public-example tasks excluded. Not cherry-picked, and small enough that no single task's outcome should be quoted on its own.

arms.control: --control, official config, 50-call budget (its own native setting)
arms.librecalc: --observation formula-patterns-v1 --execution formula-blocks-v1 --read-policy progressive, 12-call budget (its own native setting)

reading: A win at 12 calls against the baseline's 50 is the strong result. A loss is the more important one and must be recorded as plainly: it would mean the ISA is paying for itself in constraint rather than capability.
